slides.title: Telling Timeless Tales
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 5 English, Unit 4: Telling Timeless Tales. Unit 4 explores myths and legends, the timeless tales families have retold for centuries. You will read an information text about the two forms, the legend of the Whispering Dunes, and the three-part desert adventure "The Hasty Route". You will study twenty-five describing words, from hasty and reluctant to justifiable and prosperous, in four groups. The language focus is the defining relative clause, supported by present continuous for arranged plans, comparative adjectives, opposites and verb-noun collocations, and the unit closes with you writing an original legend of your own. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Explain the difference between a myth and a legend.
Identify the key features of classic tales: oral tradition, timeless settings, moral or explanatory purpose, and larger-than-life characters.
Use defining relative clauses to add essential information to your sentences.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to explain the difference between a myth and a legend. You will also identify the key features of classic tales: oral tradition, timeless settings, moral or explanatory purpose, and larger-than-life characters. You will also use defining relative clauses to add essential information to your sentences. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Language for precise thinking
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: hasty, reluctant, furious, anxious, grateful, irritable. Listen to each pronunciation in the vocabulary lab, study its meaning in context, and use the word accurately in your own discussion and writing.

slides.title: Read critically
bullets: Myths and Legends: What Makes a Tale Timeless
The Legend of the Whispering Dunes
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes Myths and Legends: What Makes a Tale Timeless and The Legend of the Whispering Dunes. Read actively. Identify each text's central ideas, notice viewpoint and reliability, and support every inference with relevant evidence from the text.

slides.narration: The first language focus is What a Defining Relative Clause Does. A defining relative clause is a group of words that tells the reader exactly which person, place or thing the sentence means. Remove it and the sentence loses the information the reader needs. Notice the structure in the model examples, then apply it deliberately in connected sentences and paragraphs.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Explain, support and improve your ideas
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1: Retell a Legend. Organise your ideas, use evidence and respond clearly to questions. In writing, you will plan, draft, check and revise. Use the success criteria before submitting your work.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the vocabulary lab, continue through reading and comprehension, apply the grammar focus, and complete the speaking and writing practices. Use the AI tutor for hints and feedback any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
